# AgentCore harness-command-shell — AUDITED 2026-09-26 (FIRST AUDIT). [REPORTED]
# Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/harness-command-shell.html

InvokeAgentRuntimeCommandShell = persistent interactive BASH terminal inside the harness
session microVM, over WebSocket.
  wss://bedrock-agentcore.<region>.amazonaws.com/runtimes/<url-encoded-HARNESS-arn>/ws/shells
  Harness ARN required; the managed Runtime ARN is REJECTED (ValidationException).

AUTH — two independent paths:
  * SigV4 / SigV4 pre-signed URL => needs IAM bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommandShell
  * *** BEARER TOKEN => "Bearer-token requests must satisfy the harness inbound authorizer
    instead." No IAM action is evaluated on that path. ***
  Browser clients that cannot set an Authorization header pass the token INSIDE
  Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: base64UrlBearerAuthorization.<base64url-token> + the
  base64UrlBearerAuthorization sentinel. => a bearer token travels in a WebSocket
  subprotocol header value.

*** LOGGING BLIND SPOT (verbatim): "AgentCore sends the request ID and connection metadata
    to the harness Runtime log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. The service doesn't log
    terminal input or output." and "AWS CloudTrail records InvokeAgentRuntimeCommandShell
    API calls, including the caller identity, timestamp, source IP address, resolved
    Runtime resource, and response status. CloudTrail doesn't log terminal input or
    output." ***
    => connection is auditable, COMMANDS ARE NOT. Same blind spot class as
       InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand.

Security note (verbatim): "A principal that can open a Harness shell has interactive
  command access to the harness session." "The shell can access customer-provided data,
  files, and secrets in the selected environment or on mounted filesystems. It can also
  connect to network destinations that the session can reach. The shell environment uses
  an allowlist and doesn't inject AgentCore platform or workload credentials."
  Stays inside the session microVM; no cross-customer access.
  NOTE: this shell does NOT state root/uid 0 (unlike InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand, which
  harness-environment documents as running as ROOT).

BINARY FRAME PROTOCOL — first byte = channel:
  0x00 STDIN (c->s) | 0x01 STDOUT = PTY, stdout+stderr COMBINED (s->c)
  0x02 STDERR = service/platform diagnostics only (s->c)
  0x03 STATUS = UTF-8 JSON {kind,apiVersion,metadata:{shellId,reconnected,bytesDropped},status}
  0x04 RESIZE {"width":n,"height":n} 1..1000 | 0x05 HEARTBEAT (echoed) | 0xFF CLOSE
  Text frames not part of protocol; 5 consecutive text frames => close 1003.

RECONNECT / DETACH:
  ?shellId=<id> + same runtime session ID. Process KEEPS RUNNING while detached.
  Service replays up to 256 KB of buffered output; metadata.bytesDropped if it overflowed.
  *** A second connection with the same shellId REPLACES the first; the evicted client
      gets close code 4000. => shell-session hijack/takeover primitive for any principal
      holding the same permission. ***

QUOTAS: 64 KB max frame | 250 frames/sec | 1 hour max connection | 10 concurrent ACTIVE
  shells per harness session (DETACHED shells do NOT count) | 20 retained active+detached
  entries, oldest detached evicted | 256 KB replay buffer.
  Runtime session ID must be >= 33 characters.
Close codes: 1000 clean, 1003 text frames, 1006 network, 1008 duration/rate/buffer,
  1009 frame >64KB, 1011 server, 4000 replaced by another client.
Errors: ValidationException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException,
  ServiceQuotaExceededException(429), RuntimeClientError(424), ThrottlingException,
  RetryableConflictException(409).

Custom container: shell runs INSIDE that container; requires Bash at /bin/bash.
  sh and dash are NOT supported.
AgentCore CLI and high-level SDK shell helpers DO NOT support harness targets at launch.
